metadata.name: jpui-dropdown
metadata.description: A dropdown / popover container. Two dropzones: `triggerLayout` holds whatever opens it, `dropdownLayout` holds the floating panel. Opens on click, hover, or right-click; positions on any of the four sides with start/center/end alignment and px/% offsets. The panel is teleported to `#app` and positioned `fixed`, so a parent's `overflow` never clips it, and it is repositioned on scroll, window resize, and trigger resize. Both dropzones must be filled — an empty `triggerLayout` leaves nothing to click.
features: Click, hover, or right-click trigger modes
Configurable position (top, right, bottom, left) and alignment (start, center, end)
Customizable X and Y offsets in px or %
Optional slide + scale animation with transform origin derived from position and alignment
Teleported to `#app` so parent overflow never clips the panel
Repositions on scroll of any scrollable ancestor, on window resize, and on trigger resize
Nested dropdown support — a child does not close its parents
Closes on outside click or outside right-click, so opening one right-click menu closes any other open dropdown; closes on Escape; `closeDropdown` action for workflows
Open state and configuration exposed to the formula editor via local context
Responsive: on any non-default breakpoint, click opens the dropdown whatever the trigger type (right-click mode can opt out with `smallScreenClickFallback`)
`forceDisplayEditor` pins the panel open on the editor canvas for styling

properties.name: triggerType
properties.description: Type of interaction that opens the dropdown. 'click' toggles on click, 'hover' opens on mouse enter and closes 200ms after mouse leave, 'right-click' toggles on context menu. On any non-default breakpoint, plain click takes over for all three modes and hover is disabled.

properties.name: smallScreenClickFallback
properties.description: Only shown when `triggerType` is 'right-click'. When true (default), a plain click also opens the dropdown on any non-default breakpoint, since touch screens have no right-click. Set to false when the trigger's own click does something else (e.g. selecting an item); the dropdown then only opens on `contextmenu`, which Android fires on long-press but iOS Safari does not.

properties.name: position
properties.description: Side of the trigger the panel is placed on. There is no collision detection: the panel does not flip or shift when it would overflow the viewport.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: Alignment along the cross axis. For position top/bottom: start=left, center=centered, end=right. For position left/right: start=top, center=centered, end=bottom.

properties.name: offsetX
properties.description: Horizontal gap between the trigger and the panel, as a string with unit (e.g. '10px' or '5%'). No configured default; treated as '0px' when unset.

properties.name: offsetY
properties.description: Vertical gap between the trigger and the panel, as a string with unit (e.g. '8px' or '2%'). No configured default; treated as '0px' when unset.

properties.name: dropdownZIndex
properties.description: Z-index of the teleported panel, 0-100. Falls back to `unset` when empty.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: When true, blocks every trigger mode so the dropdown cannot be opened. Does not close an already-open dropdown on its own.

properties.name: animated
properties.description: When true, the panel opens and closes with a slide + scale transition. Duration (0.2s) and easing are fixed.

properties.name: closeOnEscape
properties.description: When true, pressing Escape anywhere in the page closes the dropdown. Every open instance listens, so an open parent and its nested child close together.

properties.name: closeOnContentClick
properties.description: When true, any click inside the panel closes the dropdown, after the clicked element's own click workflow has started — menu items need no close action. Clicks on a nested dropdown's trigger inside the panel are ignored so the child can open. Disabled while editing on the canvas so elements can be selected.

properties.name: forceDisplayEditor
properties.description: Editor-only. Pins the panel open on the canvas so `dropdownLayout` can be styled. Not bindable and has no effect in production.

localContext.description: Open state and resolved configuration of the dropdown, available to anything inside either dropzone as `context.local.data['dropdown']`. This is the only way to react to the dropdown opening or closing, since the component emits no trigger events.

isOpen.description: Whether the dropdown is currently open. Ignores editor force-display.

trigger.description: `{ type: 'click' | 'hover' | 'right-click', disabled: boolean }` — the resolved `triggerType` and `disabled` properties.

position.description: `{ placement, alignment, offsetX, offsetY }` — the resolved placement properties, with '0px' substituted for unset offsets.

state.description: `{ isDisplayed: boolean, isAnimated: boolean }`. `isDisplayed` is true when the panel is rendered, including when it is only shown because of `forceDisplayEditor` in the editor.

actions.label: Close dropdown
actions.description: Programmatically closes the dropdown. There is no matching open action.

slots.name: triggerLayout
slots.description: The element(s) that open the dropdown. Clicking, hovering, or right-clicking this area (depending on `triggerType`) toggles the panel. Must contain at least one element, otherwise there is nothing to interact with.

slots.name: dropdownLayout
slots.description: The floating panel content, mounted only while the dropdown is open. Can contain any elements — menus, lists, forms, nested dropdowns. Give it its own background and elevation; the component adds no styling of its own.

specifications: The panel is teleported to the `#app` element of the front document and positioned `fixed` from the trigger's bounding box, so a parent's `overflow: hidden` never clips it.
Position is recomputed on scroll of every scrollable ancestor of the trigger, on window resize, and on trigger resize via a ResizeObserver — but only while the dropdown is displayed.
No collision detection: the panel never flips or shifts to stay inside the viewport. Choose or bind a `position` that fits.

On any non-default breakpoint, a plain click opens the dropdown regardless of `triggerType`, and hover is disabled — this makes hover and right-click usable on touch devices. In right-click mode, `smallScreenClickFallback: false` disables the plain-click fallback.
The trigger calls preventDefault on `contextmenu` in every trigger mode, so right-clicking the trigger never shows the browser's native menu, even when `triggerType` is 'click' or 'hover'.
In hover mode, leaving the trigger or the panel closes after a 200ms delay so the pointer can cross the gap between them.
The teleported node is unmounted 250ms after closing, to let the leave transition finish.

Clicking or right-clicking outside both the trigger and the panel closes the dropdown, so right-clicking a second context-menu trigger closes the first menu. In hover mode on the default breakpoint the outside-click handler is skipped.
Nested dropdowns are supported: each instance registers its id with its ancestors, and the outside-click handler ignores clicks inside any registered trigger or panel.
In the editor, hover never opens the dropdown but click still does. Use `forceDisplayEditor` to keep the panel pinned open while styling it.
`forceDisplayEditor` only affects editor mode preview and has no effect in production.
Exposes no trigger events — watch `context.local.data['dropdown']['isOpen']` to react to open/close.
Exposes no component variable; open state lives only in local context.
Does not support programmatic open — only the `closeDropdown` action is available.
Animation timing is fixed at 0.2s ease; duration and easing are not configurable.

No ARIA or focus management: the trigger is a plain div with no role or aria-expanded and the panel is not focus-managed. Escape closes it unless `closeOnEscape` is off. Add accessible semantics inside the dropzones if needed.

examples.description: A click-triggered menu below the trigger, left-aligned, with an 8px gap and animation. `forceDisplayEditor` is on so the panel can be styled on the canvas.
A hover-triggered panel to the right of the trigger, vertically centered, with a small gap.
A right-click context menu anchored to the bottom-left of the cursor's element, above other content.
